question: With the rise of online learning platforms, some argue that traditional classroom education is becoming obsolete. To what extent do you agree or disagree?
essay:
The proliferation of online learning platforms has led some observers to claim that conventional classroom instruction is no longer relevant. While I acknowledge the considerable advantages of digital education, I disagree that it renders traditional teaching obsolete.

Those who argue for the redundancy of classrooms point to convenience and cost. Online courses allow learners to study at their own pace, revisit recorded material, and access world-class instructors regardless of geography. For working adults in particular, this flexibility removes barriers that would otherwise make further study impossible.

Nevertheless, physical classrooms deliver benefits that screens cannot replicate. Spontaneous discussion, immediate correction from a teacher who can read confusion on a student's face, and the discipline imposed by a fixed schedule all contribute to deeper learning. Moreover, for younger learners, school provides socialisation that is arguably as important as academic content. Laboratory work, clinical training and performance arts simply cannot be conducted remotely.

In my view, the most effective model is a blended one in which online resources handle knowledge transmission while classroom time is reserved for discussion and practice. Rather than replacing traditional education, technology should be understood as an instrument that reshapes it.
